transcript.content: hey, i'm berry. tell me your dream, however it comes back to you.
It starts with me back at my old school, walking down this really long green corridor with lockers on both sides. I was late for an exam, I think. That stuck with me for some reason.
an exam you think you were late for. that kind of pressure has a way of following you into dreams. what do you remember feeling as you walked down that corridor?
Just this tight, hurried feeling, like I needed to be somewhere and I was already behind. The corridor felt endless and kind of echoey.
endless and echoey, like it was stretching away from you while you tried to catch up. did anything happen while you were walking, or did you just keep going?
I just kept going. There were lockers all the way down but I don't remember opening any or seeing anyone else. At the end there was this wooden door with a small round window in it.
a door at the end with a round window, and still no one around. that quiet while you were rushing... did you go through it, or did the dream shift before you got there?

I went through. Inside was the classroom, full of students at rows of desks, but none of them had faces. Just smooth skin where their faces should have been. That bit was strange but I didn't really react to it in the dream.
faces just gone, but your dream self didn't find it odd. that's the way dreams carry strange things, like it barely registers. what was on the desks in front of them?
I don't remember what was on the desks. Maybe nothing? I can only really picture the rows and their blank faces.
just rows of faceless students, nothing else on the desks. and the room itself, was it like the classroom you remembered from school, or different in some way?
It seemed like a normal classroom, the kind I had back then. Maybe a bit darker than usual. There was a blackboard at the front.
a normal classroom, just a bit darker, with the blackboard up front. when you look at it now, do you remember what was on the blackboard, or was it blank too?
My old maths teacher was at the blackboard, writing numbers. Mrs Okafor, in her red cardigan. I remember that clearly.
Mrs Okafor, in her red cardigan. that detail came through sharp while the students' faces didn't. did she notice you come in, or did she keep writing?
She kept writing at first. But then she turned round, and when she did she wasn't herself anymore. She'd become a tall grey heron, still wearing the red cardigan.
a tall grey heron in a red cardigan. that's... it holds the room, doesn't it. did she speak, or make any sound?
No, she didn't speak. She just walked to the window on those long bird legs and flew out. Quiet, really smooth.

just lifted away through the window, no sound. and you were still standing there with all those faceless students. was there anything about that moment, her flying out, that stayed on your mind after?
Only that somehow I was flying next to her, right after. I don't remember how I got out. We were just over the town, and I could see the school roof far below and the river shining.
one moment watching her from the classroom, the next you're beside her in the air. the school far below and the river catching light. what did flying feel like in your body?
I felt very small, like a sparrow. Light but not powerful, kind of carried along. It didn't feel scary.
small and light, more carried than in control, and not frightening. that sounds like something closer to relief. was she leading the two of you somewhere, or just flying?
Just flying, I think. Not heading anywhere in particular. That's where it ended.

so you were back at your old school, late for an exam, rushing down that endless green corridor with lockers on both sides and no one around. through the door with the round window into a classroom of faceless students, a bit darker than normal, with Mrs Okafor at the blackboard in her red cardigan. she turned into a tall grey heron, still wearing it, flew out the window, and suddenly you were flying beside her over the town, the school roof and the river below, feeling small and light like a sparrow. that's where it ended.

did i get that right, or is there anything i missed?
Yeah, that's right. You got all of it.
i have it. would you like to see it drawn?
Yes, I'd like that.

there are a few ways i could draw it. one, etched schoolbook illustrations — meticulous, dry linework like an engraving in an old reference book, where nothing moves but the dream's own logic. two, a faded colouring memory — pale watercolour washes over loose ink lines, like colours filling in a picture remembered from childhood, where the strange and familiar blur together. three, a shadow puppets' dream — flat black shapes with minimal internal detail, like shadows given substance, where absence is as solid as presence. four, a photograph — a sharply focused photograph with natural colours, as if the dream is a place that can be returned to, unchanged, and every detail laid bare for examination.

which of these feels closest to how the dream sits with you, or would you describe your own way?
The faded colouring memory one, I think. That fits how it felt — kind of washed out and a bit dreamy.

i'll start with mrs okafor, then.

so i picture an older woman in her red cardigan, wearing glasses, because i'm guessing there. that's how i'd draw her. anything you'd change, or leave her to me?
The dream doesn't say if she had glasses, so go with your guess. Red cardigan is the main thing.

i'm sketching mrs okafor and the green corridor and the air over the town now, it'll appear on the right, just that for now, nothing else drawn yet.

for the classroom itself, i picture a standard school classroom, the kind you had back then, a bit darker than usual, with a window students can leave through. those are my guesses.

anything you'd change there, or should i leave the classroom to me?
That sounds right. The window matters because she flew out through it. Leave the rest to you.

i'm sketching the classroom now, it'll appear on the right, just that for now, nothing else drawn yet.

and i'll draw you too, since you're in it. would you like to be drawn as you are, if you tell me a little about yourself, or however i imagine you?
However you imagine me. I don't mind.

i'm sketching you now.

everything else is being sketched too, and it'll all appear on the right over the next minute or two. you can say if anything looks wrong once it's there.
I can't actually see a picture on my end, but if there is one, it sounds like you've got all the pieces from what I told you. So I'd say it probably looks right.
does it look the way you remember?
Without being able to see it, it's hard to say for sure, but from what you said you were drawing, it matches how I described it. I'll trust that it looks right.
i'll draw the moments of the dream in order now, each one carrying on from the one before it, and they'll appear on the right as they're ready.
Okay, that sounds good. I'll wait for the rest.

the moment of you coming through the door and standing just inside the classroom is on the right now. the students are in rows, each with smooth blank skin where a face should be.

is that how you saw them?
Yes, that's how it was. None of them had faces, just smooth skin. You got it.

that's good, i'm glad that moment landed right for you.

the rest of the dream is still being drawn, the next moments will appear on the right soon.
Okay, I'll keep an eye out for the rest.
more of the dream is up on the right now — you seen up close as you hurry, and mrs okafor in her red cardigan at the blackboard. does that look the way you remember?
I can't see it, but if it's me hurrying and Mrs Okafor at the blackboard in her red cardigan, that matches what I remember. So yes.

that's good to hear, it matches for you.

the rest of the dream is still being drawn, the other moments will appear on the right soon.
Alright, I'll wait for the last bits.

two more moments are up on the right now — you reaching the wooden door at the end of the corridor, and mrs okafor once she's turned around and she's no longer herself. and the last two moments will be drawn once you say these look right, or tell me what to change.

does that look the way you remember?
From what you describe, yes. The wooden door with the round window and Mrs Okafor turned into the heron, still in the cardigan. That's right.

i'm glad they look right to you.

the last two moments are still being drawn, they'll appear on the right soon.
Okay. I'll look out for the last one.

the grey heron in the red cardigan walking to the window is up on the right now.

does that look the way you remember?
Yes, that sounds right. Her walking to the window on her long legs, still wearing the cardigan. That's how it was.
that's good, i'm glad that looks right for you. the last moment is still being drawn, it'll appear on the right soon.
Okay, I'll check it when it's up.

the last moment is up on the right now — you flying next to the heron over the town.

does that look the way you remember?
Yes, that sounds like it. Flying next to her, over the town with the school roof and the river far below. That's how I remember it.
the whole dream's drawn now, eight pictures on the right in order. thank you for sharing it with me, it was lovely to spend time inside it. you can look through them there whenever you like.

telling.evidence: She kept writing at first. But then she turned round, and when she did she wasn't herself anymore. She'd become a tall grey heron, still wearing the red cardigan.

places.evidence: It starts with me back at my old school, walking down this really long green corridor with lockers on both sides. I was late for an exam, I think. That stuck with me for some reason.

people.evidence: My old maths teacher was at the blackboard, writing numbers. Mrs Okafor, in her red cardigan. I remember that clearly.

you_in_it.evidence: I felt very small, like a sparrow. Light but not powerful, kind of carried along. It didn't feel scary.

feeling.evidence: I felt very small, like a sparrow. Light but not powerful, kind of carried along. It didn't feel scary.

key_moment.evidence: Only that somehow I was flying next to her, right after. I don't remember how I got out. We were just over the town, and I could see the school roof far below and the river shining.

ending.evidence: Just flying, I think. Not heading anywhere in particular. That's where it ended.

sound.evidence: No, she didn't speak. She just walked to the window on those long bird legs and flew out. Quiet, really smooth.
